note: Every entry is an original proposed requirement; mapping implies coverage/ownership, not adoption or implementation. Residuals are conditional after F1–F7, not current extra gaps.

requirements.statement: Formal glossary with type disjointness and permitted relations: Agent owns Workflow; Command resolves Workflow; Workflow requests Capability; Tool implements Capability; Run instantiates Workflow; Module extends Agent; Agent may delegate to another independently registered Agent.
Immutable `agentId`, version, contractVersion, schemaVersion, revision/digest, status, activation policy and declared responsible principal.
First-class admission test: mandate, independent lifecycle and accountable control boundary; avoid converting named procedures into agents.
Separate `agent_definition`, `runtime_deployment`, `identity_principal`, `workload_instance` and `run` identities.
Versioned compatibility declarations and immutable historical versions.
Machine-readable and human-readable discoverability/description without treating description as authority.
Documentation card for purpose, intended users, known limitations, prohibited applications, test profile and change history.
Explicit mandate issuer, subject, allowable action kind/resource target, issued/expiry times, revocation pointer, non-goals and signed/verifiable proof where supported.
Principal–agent–tool delegation linkage; downstream rights are attenuated, never amplified.
Zero/least standing privilege; just-in-time credential binding and expiration/rotation.
Policy decision interface distinct from model planner, including signed/pinned policy, decision expiry, deny reasons and obligations.
Target/resource-level checks for read **and** write; a read may be sensitive even if no mutation occurs.
Multidimensional risk/effect classification: action class, data sensitivity, recipients, reversibility, financial impact, blast radius, network exposure, retention/jurisdiction.
Deterministic independent human-review triggers, approval request package and expiration; no approval inferred from prompt text.
Revocation/fail-closed behavior before consequential effects and after pause/resume.
Cross-tenant isolation and user-consent boundaries with provenance.
Authorization-denial evidence emitted for attempts, including service unavailable/indeterminate outcomes, with privacy safeguards.
Optional typed model-adapter binding and provider-agnostic interface, version, provenance/hash, supported modalities and sampling behavior.
Versioned instructions/prompts and their precedence; separately controlled developer configuration vs untrusted source content.
Strategy interface: direct response, plan-and-act, ReAct-style interleaving, deterministic sequential/parallel routing, reflective loop, evaluator–optimizer; none is compulsory.
Bounded plan graph with objectives, assumptions, steps, dependencies, expected outcome and allowed tool/capability IDs.
Max reasoning cycles, max tool calls, recursion/delegation depth, context and token budgets; absolute timeout and cancellation triggers.
Grounding/fact-verification and uncertainty/abstention policy; input confidence is never authorization.
Separate synthesis, checking and authorized finalization. No model-generated self-assertion of acceptance.
Fallback/model substitution rules require regression against the approved model binding, not a silent upgrade.
Version-pinned Command→Workflow mapping; declared inputs and outputs as JSON Schema, with semantic validation beyond schema.
Workflow step graph, dependency and concurrency boundaries, finite stopping conditions and terminal-state map.
Typed capability registry with implementation adapter, action kind, target scope, authentication scopes, quotas, failure codes and availability state.
Tool schema version, deterministic validation, tool-call allowlist, output contract, error semantics, trusted/untrusted provenance and content redaction.
Transaction envelope: preview → authorize → execute → reconcile for impactful actions; dry-run where supported.
Decompose input-source instructions from operational authority; prompt injection from tool response cannot rewrite command/mandate.
Explicit human input/approval resumability; approval is separately authenticated, scoped and time-bounded.
Inter-agent invocation is optional and must define identity, delegation, context minimization, capability negotiation and task-state contracts.
Declare context assembly strategy, token budgets, truncation/compaction and provenance; do not treat a long model window as guaranteed retrieval.
Differentiate ephemeral context, short-term run/thread state, long-term episodic/semantic memory, retrieval indexes, shared knowledge and authoritative domain data.
Memory stores are typed, versioned, scoped, access-controlled, attributable and default disabled if not configured.
Memory write admission, source trust rank, retention/expiry, revalidation, correction, deletion/erasure and poisoning defense.
Retrieval quality checks: relevance, provenance, recency, contradictory claims, source access and no instruction injection.
Explicit context handoff and summarization with fidelity tests and privacy minimization.
No learned/remembered statement can bypass a rule, tool permission or human decision.
Separate session/conversation, task, run, step, event, approval, receipt and deployment identities.
State machine with legal transitions, monotonic event history, optimistic concurrency/leases and cancellation.
Checkpoints, resume, retry/replay boundaries, idempotency keys for external writes and dead-letter/reconciliation states.
Effect execution and outcome uncertainty must be modeled explicitly: PREPARED/AUTHORIZED/EXECUTING/COMMITTED/UNKNOWN, as applicable.
External effects cannot be assumed exactly-once merely because the workflow runner is durable. Use idempotent downstream APIs, transaction/outbox/saga/compensation when appropriate.
Crash recovery, worker fencing, lease expiry, backpressure, queue limits, poison task quarantine and bounded retries.
Safe suspension/kill switch that prevents queued, running and resumed work from exceeding currently valid authority.
Reproducible replay of **control events**, while accepting that stochastic model output may not reproduce byte-for-byte.
Threat model covering tool misuse, prompt injection, goal hijack, credential abuse, memory/context poisoning, cross-agent communication, rogue delegation, cascading failures and untrusted code.
Network/file/secret compartmentalization; sandbox code execution, no ambient shell/FS access without explicit capability.
Source trust labels for every untrusted input, tool result, retrieved document, memory and external skill; deny instruction laundering.
Tool and protocol OAuth resource/audience validation, token separation, refresh policies, least privilege and no token passthrough.
Secure import of prompts/skills/tool packages with integrity pin, provenance, review and SBOM where appropriate.
Restrict sensitive logs; classify/redact PII, credentials, prompts, retrieved records, chain-of-thought or private system instructions as required.
Data residency, retention, deletion, tenant isolation and consent controls as host-linked policy profiles.
Emergency disable, incident severity, forensics and evidence integrity.
Supply-chain provenance for deployed runtime and tool dependencies; approved plugin/skill update mechanism.
Do not treat model guardrails as substitutes for deterministic authorization.
Evaluation taxonomy: contract, authorization, binding, execution correctness, evidence integrity, regression, safety/adversarial, performance, human usability and deployment.
Reference datasets with provenance/version, representative positive/negative edge cases and domain-owned gold-state checks.
Assess final environment state and side-effects, not only textual outputs. Test tool names, arguments, timing, target and rollback.
Multi-run reliability (including pass^k or equivalent), variance, random seed/config metadata, flakiness and inter-run drift.
Independent human calibration of model-based graders; graders are neither self-certifying nor sufficient for effect authorization.
Adversarial tests for untrusted tool outputs, memory poisoning, delegation amplification, confirmation fatigue, tool response tampering and replay.
Measure task success, policy violations, recovery, completion latency, token/currency cost, throughput and resource consumption.
Gate promotion via explicit thresholds and complete evidence, with severities and waiver policy; failure cannot be hidden as warning.
Record evaluation environment/model/tool versions, dataset digest, code revision, sample size and confidence limitations.
End-to-end correlation across principal, agent, workflow, task, run, step, policy decision, tool call and output artifact.
Typed spans/events for agent, workflow, planner, model, retrieval, memory and tools; OTel semantic conventions usable as optional export mapping.
Append-only decision/effect ledger with before/after receipts and ambiguous outcome classification.
Preserve input and output artifact digests, source, creator, version, access basis, transformation and verification links.
Audit trail independent of mutable session memory; retention/erasure mechanisms must balance privacy with legally required audit retention.
Record tool/token/cost/latency metrics with missing/unknown semantics; zero and unknown must not be confused.
Redaction and sampling policy is separate from proof-required evidence; sampling telemetry cannot remove mandatory audit records.
Reconciliation receipts and independent acceptance references.
Health/readiness/liveness contracts, degraded modes, dependency and model-provider outage behavior.
Quotas, per-run/per-principal cost ceiling, rate limits, concurrency controls, admission control and circuit breakers.
SLOs for correct task completion, latency, availability, stalled jobs, denial accuracy and evidence completeness.
Inventory, health, drift, vulnerability, registry integrity and unsupported version audit interfaces.
No self-upgrade into production: signed release/provenance, migration plan, rollback, canary/shadow strategy and independent promotion.
Incident/forensic record, emergency suspension, recovery procedure and notification/escalation obligations.
Tenancy and data segregation across persistent state, credentials, telemetry and tool results.
Generic adapter interface for model provider, tool execution, policy decision, identity, memory, event bus and data store.

MCP: optional tool/resource/prompt endpoint; if implemented against 2026-07-28, support stateless core, per-request version/capabilities, explicit state handle, tool schemas and transport authorization; Tasks as separately negotiated extension.
A2A: optional externally discoverable agent API, Agent Card, task/multimodal negotiation, authentication, streaming and cancellation; **not** the internal registry schema.
OpenAPI/JSON Schema: typed I/O and reference resolution; validation does not encode all semantic constraints.
OpenTelemetry: optional exporter and stable custom application event IDs; agent/workflow/tool span conventions currently Development.
Extensible skills/packages via declared schema, integrity pins and bounded capability expansion only after approval.
Protocol-version negotiation, deprecation windows, compatibility tests and security regression.
Agent card: intended use, restrictions, capabilities, known limitations, evidence/benchmarks, deployment and incident contact.
Risk register with purpose, affected users, potential harms, model assumptions and controls.
Governance obligations are conditional by deployment role/jurisdiction and risk; do not encode a particular statute as universal law.
Separate agent acceptance, conformance and policy approvals; record approver identity and jurisdiction.
Human oversight designed for meaningful review, not habituated click-through; escalation includes context, alternatives and likely effects.
Signed audit, release and incident/change provenance where required.
Clear ownership for lifecycle, authority, policies, data and tools.
